changes: Automation JSON state reads and atomic writes are serialized per file so Windows cannot catch NewzDeck replacing media-library.json while another NewzDeck thread still has that destination open.
Atomic JSON replacement retries short-lived Windows access/sharing violations with bounded backoff instead of immediately surfacing WinError 5 for transient file-handle contention.
Automation media Save confirms success immediately after the authoritative media update has been persisted instead of waiting for a full Automation summary rebuild.
Wanted, Calendar, health, counts, and related Automation summary state refresh asynchronously after a successful media Save.
Season and episode monitoring toggles also refresh the larger Automation summary asynchronously rather than blocking their UI handlers.
regression_guards: Automation state writes remain atomic; the fix does not fall back to in-place JSON truncation/overwrite.
The Saved notification is emitted only after /api/automation/media/update returns successfully, so the faster acknowledgement is not an optimistic or fake save.
The returned authoritative media item is merged into local UI state before the background Automation summary refresh.
JSON replace retries are bounded to a short window and only retry Windows permission/sharing-style failures.
v3.6.13 download continuity, verified Remove/Cancel, hidden-transfer reconciliation, Wanted policy visibility, and fallback-only season-pack arbitration remain preserved.
v3.6.12 installer-owned update restoration and prior source-freshness protections remain preserved.
name: Automation Save Reliability & Responsiveness
